summary: With no subplan you complete the General Program: 45 units of Philosophy courses numbered 100 or above, letter graded with a B- or better, the undergraduate core (logic, philosophy of science, moral and political philosophy, contemporary theoretical philosophy, two history of philosophy courses, which do not count toward the 45 units), three graduate core areas, two PHIL courses numbered 200 or above (not graduate sections of undergraduate courses), and three courses in one specialization area. The Symbolic Systems and Philosophy of Language subplans replace it with their own required courses and allow 9 of the 45 units from the field of specialization. Checked by hand: area and history courses without a Bulletin list, which you move in, and in Symbolic Systems the spread of your graduate and outside courses across areas.

RI8pDAnO.why: subplanRequired is false: a student in neither special program (Symbolic Systems, Philosophy of Language) completes the General Program, so it applies only with no subplan. The Philosophy of Language text treats the General Program's undergraduate core as something its students "may be required to satisfy", so the programs are alternatives.

SfheeWvb.why: "Each program requires a minimum of 45 units in philosophy. Students in a special program may be allowed or required to replace up to nine units of philosophy with nine units in the field of specialization ... At least 45 units in courses numbered 100 or above must be completed with a B- or better grade at Stanford." The 45 is program.unitsMin; for the General Program the unit, level and grade rule is encoded in uVXJgSXV.

uVXJgSXV.why: "The General Program requires a minimum of 45 units in Philosophy courses numbered above 99. These courses must be taken for a letter grade, and the student must receive at least a B- in the course." The undergraduate core does not count ("Courses taken to satisfy the undergraduate core or affiliated courses may not be counted in the 45 units"), so those rules do not share courses with this one.
